reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational Gestalt framework posits that perceptual organization arises from relational structures—specifically, means-end relations—that bind environmental fields into coherent gestalts. These gestalts are not merely sensory aggregates but sign-gestalts, encoding meaning through symbolic relations. The emphasis on purposive structure implies that each gestalt serves a functional role within an agent’s behavioral repertoire. This dualism of sign and purpose creates a kernel of embedded logic: all gestalts are structured by means-end strands, which can be modeled as directed graphs in GSI’s Bayesian framework. In GSE, these same structures evolve as state transitions driven by goal-oriented dynamics. The failure mode occurs when either sign-gestalt ambiguity or means-end disconnection undermines the integrity of the gestalt, leading to perceptual fragmentation or maladaptive behavior.
